entries.abstract: Drawing on framing theory and the social construction of target populations, this study examines whether and how landmark legislation is associated with shifts in media framing of the populations it targets. entries.title: Bureaucratic behavior in the implementation of freedom of information laws: evidence from a field experiment in Belgian municipalities
entries.abstract: Abstract Freedom of Information (FOI) laws are widely adopted to promote transparency, yet their implementation diverges from formal legal expectations. This article examines how variations in FOI requests shape administrative responses and what these patterns reveal about bureaucratic behavior in municipal administrations. Drawing on a randomized field experiment across Belgian municipalities, the study analyzes how public officials respond to identical FOI requests varying by requester identity and legal framing. The findings show that responsiveness is not neutral but varies systematically across request characteristics and contexts. Ordinary citizens receive higher disclosure rates than institutional or advocacy actors, and invoking FOI law increases compliance for some requesters while reducing it for others. entries.title: Digging Into the Subsoil: Considering and Theorizing Human Services Delivery at the Sub‐Micro‐Level of the Public Service Ecosystem
entries.abstract: ABSTRACT Public services are often delivered in partnership with families and communities, yet these relationships receive limited attention within public service ecosystem (PSE) theory. Responding to call to develop the sub‐micro‐level of the PSE, we introduce the concept of subsoil sensitivity to foreground the family and community ecosystems that underpin public service value creation. These informal systems are active sites of value creation and destruction with sensitivities arising from their alignment or misalignment with public services. We propose legislative and policy nodes as connectors that translate macrolevel policy into microlevel practice. Drawing on child protection vignettes, we show how nodes create the conditions for interaction, while subsoil dynamics influence whether value is cocreated or codestroyed amid power asymmetries and differing belief systems. entries.title: Bureaucratic behavior in the implementation of freedom of information laws: evidence from a field experiment in Belgian municipalities
entries.abstract: Abstract Freedom of Information (FOI) laws are widely adopted to promote transparency, yet their implementation diverges from formal legal expectations. This article examines how variations in FOI requests shape administrative responses and what these patterns reveal about bureaucratic behavior in municipal administrations. Drawing on a randomized field experiment across Belgian municipalities, the study analyzes how public officials respond to identical FOI requests varying by requester identity and legal framing. The findings show that responsiveness is not neutral but varies systematically across request characteristics and contexts. Ordinary citizens receive higher disclosure rates than institutional or advocacy actors, and invoking FOI law increases compliance for some requesters while reducing it for others. entries.title: Toward an “Identity Turn” in Public Service Motivation Theory: A Problematizing Review and Research Agenda
entries.abstract: Abstract Since its inception, Public Service Motivation (PSM) has been recognized as a key driver of behavior in public institutions. Despite its prominence, skepticism has emerged. In response, research has primarily focused on empirical analysis and measurement refinement rather than on conceptual development. This conceptual path dependency has become problematic as mixed empirical results increasingly challenge core theoretical propositions of PSM theory. We argue that one potential cause lies in a dominant assumption shaping the field: its positioning within motivation theory. To address this, we conducted a problematizing review across concepts and disciplines, comparing how PSM is understood in Public Administration with related concepts–such as motivation, altruism, and identity–in Management, Psychology, Sociology, and Economics.
